structuredContent.grid_recovery: Creation recovers the pixel grid the model drew with Unzoom. An exact grid is kept; drift of at most one pixel is recovered on the expected grid. Images with a background must fill the canvas, so any other size is redrawn with image-to-pixel-art on the generated box only. Sprites without a background keep their own pixels, centred on the canvas, while the drawn pixel is close to the requested one; coarser or oversized sprites are redrawn. Experimental 16x16 creation always uses image-to-pixel-art. Editing and inpainting start at 32x32 and never use image-to-pixel-art conversion.

# MCP Tool: create_image_pro_flash

Create one Pro Flash pixel-art image with an optional left-box style image.

Custom sizes (Beta) accept width and height from 16 to 256 in multiples of 4 pixels.
Query get_pro_flash_capabilities for native presets.
The style image accepts {url}, {base64}, or {source_image_id}; prefer URLs
for uploaded images. Style art must fit the native canvas without resizing.
For several assets of one game, pass the same anchor sprite as style_image on
every call (e.g. the hero's south rotation URL from get_character); without it
each call picks its own look.
style_options selects color_palette, outline, detail and shading independently.
Default style uses existing PixelLab art. For a console or palette look (1-bit,
Game Boy, PICO-8, any palette from Lospec) pass `palette` as its hex colours plus
`palette_name`: the image is drawn for the palette and every pixel of the result
is one of its colours; the style image keeps lending its look. Returns one image.
Failed pixel grids use image-to-pixel-art with fixer on the generated box.
Poll get_image(job_id); use source_image_id after completion.

Cost: by LONGEST SIDE — 5 generations up to 96px, 6 from 100 to 208, 9 from
212 to 256, for one image. A non-square canvas goes by its longer side, so
128x72 is 6 and 32x96 is 5. This is the whole Pro Flash ladder (create, edit
and inpaint charge the same), and it is NOT the Pro tools' 10/15/25 tier.
No parameter caps a charge, and the quote is labelled provisional rather
than a contractual cap — but the ladder above is what actually gets billed,
so treat those figures as the price.
get_pro_flash_capabilities(operation=, width=, height=) prices an exact size
for free before you spend.

## Parameters
- `description` (str, required)
- `width` (int, optional) [default: 64] — Native sizes: 16x16 (experimental), 24x24, 32x32, 32x48, 48x48, 64x64, 96x64, 96x96, 128x128. Custom size (Beta): integer width 16–256 and height 16–256. Both dimensions must be multiples of 4 pixels. Pixel-grid recovery uses image-to-pixel-art with fixer when needed. No native image resizing.
- `height` (int, optional) [default: 64]
- `no_background` (bool, optional) [default: True]
- `style_image` (Optional[ProFlashReferenceInput], optional) [default: None] — Style anchor. Exactly ONE of its three sources: `url` also accepts an `upload:<id>` from get_upload_url or a data: URL, and `source_image_id` is an image you own (what a Pro Flash job returns). It must fit INSIDE the output canvas both ways — a larger one is refused, so crop it; resizing pixel art is never the answer. Reuse one anchor across calls to keep a set consistent.
- `style_options` (Optional[ProFlashStyleOptions], optional) [default: None]
- `palette` (Optional[list[str]], optional) [default: None] — Target palette, 2 to 256 hex colours as a JSON array, e.g. ["#081820", "#346856", "#88c070", "#e0f8d0"] for Game Boy or ["#000000", "#ffffff"] for 1-bit. The image is drawn for these colours and every pixel of the result is one of them.
- `palette_name` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None] — Optional name of the palette (e.g. 'Game Boy', 'PICO-8'); naming it helps the look.
- `max_colors` (Optional[int], optional) [default: None] — At most this many colours in the image (2-64). With a palette, they are picked from it.
- `seed` (int, optional) [default: 0]
- `project_id` (Optional[str], optional) [default: None]

## Usage
```python
create_image_pro_flash(
    description=...,
)
```
